source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Spare mode intentionally reserves memory, yet Criteria require BIOS available size to equal installed size without defining physical/reserved/usable values; DC/warm reboot are required only in Criteria and lack procedure details.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Mode specification, capacity equation, operator and reboot/stress policy can be supplied; the pending decision does not block later review.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row42 Wistron-Memory-00025-V002: define authoritative BIOS Spare-mode label/evidence, configured-versus-activated behavior, DIMM/rank/channel placement and installed-versus-reserved-versus-BIOS/OS-usable capacity equation instead of available-equals-installed wording; specify Criteria-only DC/warm-reboot count/order and approved two-hour stress tool/workload, health/thermal/power/ECC/OOM aborts, baseline-log preservation, restore/recovery and invalid-run policy; dmesg spare/rank keywords or edac-util alone must not prove Spare mode.

review_improvement: Makes the reserved-capacity model explicit and restores direct BIOS, reboot and stress coverage beyond generic kernel keywords.
independent_technical_reasoning: Spare mode removes a platform-defined rank or capacity from normal allocation so it can replace a failing region. Therefore physical installed, reserved spare, firmware available and Linux usable memory are distinct quantities. A dmesg word match can describe capability or an event without proving current configuration; direct BIOS state and a platform capacity equation are required.
